newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MPs approve new code of conduct for lobbyists.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve new code of conduct for lobbyists.

text.p: The European Parliament on Tuesday approved a binding code of conduct for the estimated 3,000 lobbyists vying for Euro-MPs' attention.
The code, proposed by British Socialist Glyn Ford, obliges lobbyists to inform Euro-MPs whom they represent and bans them from trying to gain access to Euro-MPs under false pretences.
It also bans lobbyists from selling parliamentary documents to other people or claiming to have an official relationship with parliament.
Anyone found breaking the rules, which come into force on May 28, will be refused an entry pass to the parliament's buildings in Brussels and Strasbourg.
The code is a step forward since last July, when the parliament approved hotly disputed rules on Euro-MPs' conduct, but it still leaves a number of grey areas.

For example, it says lobbyists can no longer give crates of whisky or other gifts to Euro-MPs but they can continue to offer assistance in cash or kind, such as funding a fact-finding mission to another country or financing a Euro-MP's staff.

Ford said the new rules would force members to declare any assistance they got from lobbyists in a public register, so while they could continue to take all-expenses-paid trips to Indonesia, Taiwan or Turkey, any subsequent attempts to promote the views of the people paying for the trips would "be met by laughter, not applause."
Any deputy who failed to reveal these benefits would suffer the political costs, he warned, adding that under the new rules lobbyists would also be held responsible if the register was not correct.
